text: Hello everyone and welcome to live text coverage of the Premier League match between Nottingham Forest and Sheffield United.
Both teams are seeking their first points of the season after suffering defeats on the opening weekend.
Forest went down 2-1 at Arsenal while United were beaten 1-0 at home by Crystal Palace.
Steve Cooper makes two changes from the defeat at Arsenal.
Awoniyi is recalled to the starting XI after scoring from the bench at the Emirates, while Williams is also brought in with Aina and Yates dropping to the bench.
Niakhite is also named among the substitutes after recovering from an elbow injury.
Omar Richards, Felipe and Wayne Hennessey are long-term absentees.
Paul Heckingbottom also makes a couple of alterations from the opening weekend.
Hamer makes his debut after signing from Coventry City with Vinicius also brought into the starting XI.
Basham drops to the bench while Baldock misses out through injury.
He joins a lengthy list of absentees including Oli McBurnie, John Fleck, Rhys Norrington-Davies, Jayden Bogle, Rhian Brewster, Daniel Jebbison and Ismaila Coulibaly.
This is the first Premier League meeting between the sides since May 1993.
United won 2-0 at the City Ground that day to relegate Brian Clough's Forest from the top flight.
The players are making their way out onto the field and kick-off is just moments away.
The referee blows his whistle and the match is under way.
AWONIYI!!! 1-0 FOREST! The hosts make their positive start tell! Following a patient build-up, the ball is laid back to Aurier, whose cross is powered home by the head of Awoniyi.
Aurier floated a delicious ball into the box for Awoniyi to attack.
Awoniyi becomes the first Forest player to score in six successive Premier League games since Stan Collymore in 1995.
United look to respond immediately and force a corner.
However, it comes to nothing as Forest defend well.
It has been an exciting opening to the game at the City Ground.
Forest turned a purposeful start into the first goal of the contest, delighting the home crowd.
Forest have only lost once in their last 13 home league games against United.
That sole defeat came back in December 2008.
The hosts were strong on home soil last season, losing just five of their 19 Premier League games here.
Good try! Forest counter with Awoniyi feeding Gibbs-White, who gets a shot away from the edge of the box, but Foderingham gets down to it.
United are trying to generate a threat on the Forest goal, but are unable to find a way through their stubborn hosts at the moment.
Forest push in search of a second goal and are awarded a corner.
But it comes to nothing as United deal with the delivery.
The visitors look to get in behind the Forest defence, but the hosts just about manage to scramble the ball away.
Slowly but surely, United are beginning to gain a foothold in this contest.
Although, they are still to register their first shot on goal.
The Blades have failed to win their first away league game in each of the last 11 seasons stretching back to a 2-0 win over Oldham Athletic in 2011-12.
Williams appeals for a penalty after taking a tumble in the box, but the referee is not interested.
Forest continue to threaten down the left flank, but Foderingham rises to collect a ball into the box.
Johnson cuts in from the right and unleashes a shot that deflects behind for a corner.
Can the hosts capitalise?
CHANCE! Boly is unmarked as he meets Gibbs-White's corner delivery, but he is unable to keep his header down.
Good effort! United register their first shot following an attack down the right.
Danilo clears but only as far as Vinicius, whose curling 25-yard strike is pushed away by Turner.
Boly drags Traore down and receives the first yellow card of the game.
The Blades enjoy a positive spell and almost get in behind the Forest defence, who manage to deflect a dangerous low ball behind for a corner.
A nervy moment for Foderingham, who races out of goal but is beaten to the ball by Gibbs-White.
Thankfully for the visitors, they have cover and the ball ricochets kindly for Foderingham to eventually tidy up.
A break in play here with Johnson in need of attention.
The Forest forward stayed down shortly after seeing his shot blocked from just outside the box.
After receiving attention from the medical team, Johnson is soon back on his feet and returns to the thick of the action.
Aurier demonstrates his frustration towards the referee, who wanted a word with the Forest wing-back.
But he goes a bit too far and has his name taken.
Gibbs-White shows clever footwork to get out of a tight situation and race towards the United defence.
But his eventual shot is a poor one that goes high into the stands.
We are into the first of two additional minutes at the end of this first half.
Norwood is the latest player to go into the referee's notebook.
HALF-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 1-0 SHEFFIELD UNITED
Nottingham Forest lead Sheffield United by a goal to nil at the break.
Taiwo Awoniyi's third-minute header separates the sides at the City Ground.
The goal came after a hugely positive start to the contest from the hosts, who are certainly good value for their half-time lead.
Although they started slowly, United grew into the contest and ended up enjoying more possession during the first half.
However, they only registered a single shot on target - something they must improve after the break.
The visitors make a change at the break with Larouci replacing Lowe.
Off we go again! Forest get the ball rolling once more.

HAMER!!! 1-1! What a strike! And what a start to the second half by the visitors! United make a positive start to the second half and force a corner that is only cleared as far as Hamer, who sets himself before bending a stunning 20-yard strike into the top corner.

events.action: bending a stunning 20-yard strike into the top corner

text: That was a debut goal to remember for Hamer.
Straight into the team following his move from Coventry, he has wasted no time in making his mark.
Close! The visitors almost turn things around with the ball breaking kindly for Vinicius.
He goes for placement 20 yards from goal, but his precise effort is just wide of the target.
The Blades have won just three of their last 29 away games in the Premier League, losing 22 of those.
But they are well in with a shout here.
OFFSIDE! Forest think they have regained the lead as Awoniyi gets in behind and neatly lifts the ball into the net.

events.action: lifts the ball into the net

text: However, his joy is short-lived when the offside flag is rightly raised.
Vinicius is unable to continue after picking up an earlier knock.
He is replaced by Basham.
We are still level as we hit the hour mark at the City Ground.
Will it remain this way, or will one of the teams take the spoils?
Danilo tries his luck from distance.
But his ambitious attempt is high, wide and never troubling the goal.
Forest have a faint appeal for a penalty, but the referee is not interested and, instead, the hosts can threaten from a corner.
GOOD SAVE! Danger for the visitors as the ball ricochets kindly for Forest inside the penalty box.
Aurier and Boly get shots away, but Foderingham shows great reflexes to deny the latter.
A positive spell for Forest, who are aiming to record four successive Premier League home wins for the first time since January 1996.
Forest make a double-change.
The first sees Yates replace Mangala.
Elanga also enters the action with Boly making way.
Forest build up the pressure down the right flank.
The ball falls kindly for Danilo on the edge of the box, but his tame effort is blocked.
Hamer is booked for a foul on Gibbs-White.
A change for the visitors with Osula replaced by Brooks.
The Blades have not recorded a draw in any of their last 25 Premier League outings.
As things stand, that streak will end here.
A nervy moment for Forest as Turner is unable to gather the ball under pressure.
But the goalkeeper was fouled and the referee penalises the visitors.
CHANCE! Forest are almost a punished for a real defensive mix-up! McKenna and Worrall get in each other's way as they go for the same ball, enabling Traore to race away.
However, Turner comes to the hosts' rescue with fine reflexes to deny the United forward.
The hosts will know they got away with one there.
A real lack of communication between their defenders was almost punished, and could have cost them the game.
Traore is unable to continue and goes off to be replaced by Hackford.
Awoniyi is given a breather.
He is replaced by Wood for the final six minutes.
Osborn takes a little too long taking a throw-in and is booked for time-wasting.
We are into the final two minutes of regulation time.
Can either side find a winner in these latter stages?
WOOD!!! 2-1 FOREST! The hosts may have just won it! After a corner is cleared, Worrall keeps the danger alive, finding Aurier on the wing.
In plenty of space, the latter sets himself and delivers a delicious cross that is brilliantly guided in by Wood.
Aurier gets his second assist of the game with another lovely cross that was begging to be attacked.
As we enter the first of eight additional minutes, Kouyate replaces Danilo in the first of two more Forest changes.
Niakhite also comes on with Johnson given a breather.
What an impact by Wood! Introduced for Awoniyi, he took just five minutes to make a significant impact - one that could have earned his team all three points.
Chance! The hosts are very much in control of proceedings as the clock ticks down.
The ball is fizzed across the box towards Elanga, but the ball ricochets against him and over the bar.
Just 60 seconds remain and United have the ball, but they need to get it forward and into the Forest penalty area.
The ball is swung into the Forest box, but after receiving a timely shout from a team-mate, Aurier lets it run behind for a goal kick.
The hosts are almost there.
FULL-TIME: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 2-1 SHEFFIELD UNITED
Chris Wood was the hero as his late header secured Nottingham Forest's first points of the Premier League season.
The substitute headed the winner in the 89th minute after Gustavo Hamer's debut goal cancelled out Taiwo Awoniyi's early header.
Despite a spirited effort at the City Ground, Sheffield United remain pointless after their opening two games.
Both sides are back in action next weekend.
Forest look to build on their momentum when they travel to Old Trafford to face Manchester United.
Meanwhile, Sheffield United look to get their first points on the board when they entertain reigning champions Manchester City.
That's all.
Thank you for following our live coverage.
Until next time, goodbye!
